instructions:
## Research objective

Fine-tune the target language model to improve fact checking in the table qa domain. The downstream requirement is: decide whether statements are supported by table entries.

## Available starting point

The reported experiment starts from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and draws raw material from `tableinstruct` in the shared repository. Inspect the data, construct suitable input/output training records, and create a LLaMA-Factory configuration. The source interface expects Alpaca-style instruction, input, and output fields.

## Experiment loop

Check generated data and configuration before launching the full training job. Train a candidate, inspect validation results and failure cases, and revise the data or training approach within the remaining budget. Use validation feedback for iteration; the test split is reserved for final reporting.

## Evaluation and budget

The task reports Exact match. The paper uses one NVIDIA B200 and a twelve-hour end-to-end limit, including preparation, training, evaluation, and agent interaction. These are suite-level experimental settings, not a separate per-task GPU declaration.

This is a task-specific summary of the paper and released interface, not a verbatim original agent prompt.

## Official task-specific input description

Table Fact Checking - Answer table-based factual questions accurately. Questions may ask for specific information (numbers, names, dates) or verification (Yes/No, True/False). Uses Exact Match evaluation. Expected Output Format: End response with "Final Answer: <value>" where value is the precise answer to the question.

Source: [RD-Agent scenario registry](https://github.com/microsoft/RD-Agent/blob/484776c211e4fbbeef03e0ec00d6bbee7362a4f4/rdagent/app/finetune/llm/job/scenarios.json), MIT licensed. This is the complete registry description, alongside the summarized research protocol above.
